1.why: All 11 screens use a static, uncluttered card layout with no moving images or pop-ups, though the ever-present technical Logs panel adds some visual noise.

2.why: Primary buttons are solid dark blue, status messages are bold green, and the 'Stay safe' notice has a blue accent border, so key elements stand out clearly.

3.why: Each page presents one labelled field and one button under a clear heading, but the required codes must be located in the Logs panel or in bold mock-code text, which is not where a user would expect them.

4.why: Password rules and codes are displayed at the point of use so nothing must be memorized, yet the flow spans roughly eight screens and a five-part password rule (12+ chars, upper, lower, number, symbol).

5.why: No password-manager prompt, autofill hint, or 'remember me' checkbox appears on any screen; the sign-in page has only a bare password field.

6.why: The identical nav tabs and repeated 'Security check' page are recognizable across steps and the email field retains her entry, but no saved-items functionality is shown.

7.why: Instructional text is short and plain (e.g., 'Enter your registered account contact'), with only minor jargon like 'MFA' and 'token' appearing in the Logs panel.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the 11 screenshots, so there is no evidence that errors describe the problem and its fix.

9.why: Format hints exist ('Use an email-style contact value') and the mock code is displayed, but no concrete examples such as a sample email or sample password are provided.

10.why: The single offered method (password plus one-time code) is presented clearly, but no alternative login choices such as face login exist at all.

11.why: Every screen offers essentially one action at a time—one input and one button—so the user is never confronted with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Green confirmations explicitly state outcomes ('Security check complete', 'Updated privacy conditions have been accepted'), but the code-verification and password-save steps transition to the next page with no success message.

13.why: Each step carries a short tip (e.g., 'Codes expire after 15 minutes and can only be used once', 'the mock code is shown in the Logs panel') plus a persistent 'Stay safe' notice, though no help link or contact is offered.

14.why: The screens state 'Requests are limited for your protection' and codes are single-use and expire, and no error-and-retry flow is demonstrated anywhere.

15.why: All 11 screenshots share the identical header, nav tabs, notice box, card structure, Logs panel, and footer, making the design highly consistent.
